title: From Placeholder to Real Constraint: The OQ-01-OQ-03 Question
content: The base Wiedijk #82 formalization has `covers_unit_cube : True` — a placeholder that acknowledges cubes should cover the unit cube but does not enforce it. The OQ-01 chain proved that every nonempty dissection has a collision pair. OQ-01-OQ-03 asks: can we incorporate the geometric covering condition — specifically the volumetric necessary condition ∑ c.side³ = 1 — into the formal structure? This file answers YES by defining VolumeDissection as CubeDissection plus the volume_constraint field, then proving all the downstream consequences.
mathContext: A perfect cube dissection tiles $[0,1]^3$ with finitely many non-overlapping cubes of distinct sizes. Necessary condition: $\sum_{c \in D} (\text{side}(c))^3 = \text{vol}([0,1]^3) = 1$. The Wiedijk #82 impossibility states no such dissection exists; this file formalizes the volumetric structure without yet proving impossibility.

title: volumeSum and VolumeDissection
content: `volumeSum` computes ∑ c.side³ using Mathlib's BigOperators `∑ c ∈ cubes, c.side ^ 3`. `VolumeDissection` extends `CubeDissection` with the field `volume_constraint : volumeSum dissection.cubes = 1`, replacing the placeholder `covers_unit_cube : True` with the necessary geometric condition that cube volumes sum to 1.
mathContext: For axis-aligned cubes in ℝ³, a cube with side length $s$ has volume $s^3$. If finitely many cubes tile the unit cube $[0,1]^3$ with disjoint interiors, the volumes must sum to $\text{vol}([0,1]^3) = 1$. The constraint $\sum_{c} c.\text{side}^3 = 1$ is a necessary condition for any valid tiling.

title: Volume and Side Bounds from Constraint
content: `cube_volume_le_one` uses `Finset.single_le_sum`: since each term is nonneg and the total is 1, every individual term is ≤ 1. `cube_side_le_one` then derives `c.side ≤ 1` from `c.side³ ≤ 1` and `c.side > 0` using `nlinarith` with the hint `sq_nonneg (c.side - 1)`, which expands to `c.side² - 2·c.side + 1 ≥ 0` and enables cubic arithmetic.
mathContext: From $\sum s_i^3 = 1$ with each $s_i^3 \geq 0$, we get $s_k^3 \leq 1$ for each $k$. Since $s_k > 0$ (positivity axiom), $s_k^3 \leq 1$ implies $s_k \leq 1$. The algebraic step: if $s > 1$ then $(s-1)^2 \geq 0$ gives $s^2 \geq 2s - 1$, so $s^3 = s \cdot s^2 \geq s(2s-1) = 2s^2 - s > 2(1) - s > 1$ for $s > 1$.

title: Basic volumeSum Lemmas: Nonnegativity, Singleton, Insert
content: `volumeSum_nonneg` proves ∑ c.side³ ≥ 0 using `Finset.sum_nonneg` with `pow_nonneg` and cube side positivity. `volumeSum_singleton` specializes to {c}: ∑_{x∈{c}} x.side³ = c.side³ using `Finset.sum_singleton`. `volumeSum_insert` gives the recursion formula for adding a cube to a set: ∑_{x∈insert(c,S)} = c.side³ + ∑_{x∈S} when c ∉ S, using `Finset.sum_insert`. These are the algebraic infrastructure on which all subsequent bounds rely.
mathContext: $\text{volumeSum}(\{c\}) = c.\text{side}^3$. $\text{volumeSum}(S \cup \{c\}) = c.\text{side}^3 + \text{volumeSum}(S)$ when $c \notin S$. $\text{volumeSum}(S) \geq 0$ since each $s_i > 0$.

title: Strict Volume Bound: Each Cube Has Volume < 1 When |D| ≥ 2
content: `volumeSum_pos` establishes strict positivity of the volume sum whenever the dissection is nonempty: extract any cube `c` with `Finset.Nonempty`, note `c.side^3 > 0` via `pow_pos`, then apply `Finset.single_le_sum`. The main theorem `cube_volume_lt_one_of_card_ge_two` uses a contradiction argument: if some cube had volume exactly 1, it would exhaust the full volume budget. `Finset.one_lt_card` extracts a second distinct cube; `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg` on the pair gives `c.side³ + c'.side³ ≤ 1`, forcing `c'.side³ ≤ 0`. But `Cube.side_pos` gives `c'.side > 0`, so `c'.side³ > 0` — contradiction.
mathContext: When $|D| \geq 2$ and $\sum_{c \in D} c.\text{side}^3 = 1$, suppose $c_0.\text{side}^3 = 1$. Pick $c' \in D \setminus \{c_0\}$. Then $\{c_0, c'\} \subseteq D$ and $c_0.\text{side}^3 + c'.\text{side}^3 \leq \sum_{D} = 1$, so $c'.\text{side}^3 \leq 0$. Since $c'.\text{side} > 0$, $c'.\text{side}^3 > 0$: contradiction. Thus every cube satisfies $c.\text{side}^3 < 1$ when $|D| \geq 2$.

title: Bridging OQ-01 to Volume-Constrained Dissections
content: `volume_dissection_has_collision` is a one-line proof that calls `every_dissection_has_collision` from OQ-01 on `vd.dissection`. This demonstrates that the Wiedijk #82 impossibility result — "every cube dissection has a collision pair" — applies directly to VolumeDissection. Since VolumeDissection projects to CubeDissection, any theorem proven for all CubeDissections holds for every VolumeDissection. The two axioms underlying the collision theorem (smallest-cube and long-chains) are inherited unchanged.
mathContext: Formally: $\text{VolumeDissection} \xrightarrow{.\text{dissection}} \text{CubeDissection}$. The theorem $\text{every\_dissection\_has\_collision} : \forall d : \text{CubeDissection}, d.\text{cubes.Nonempty} \to \exists c_1\, c_2,\, \text{IsCollisionPair}\, d\, c_1\, c_2$ applies to $\text{vd.dissection}$ directly. Combined with the volume constraint: a collision pair with side $s$ must satisfy $2s^3 \leq 1$ (proved in the next section), giving $s \leq 2^{-1/3} \approx 0.794$.

title: Collision Pairs and Volume: 2s³ ≤ 1
content: `collision_volume_bound` proves that for any collision pair (c₁, c₂) — two distinct cubes with c₁.side = c₂.side = s — we have 2s³ ≤ 1. The proof: both cubes are in the dissection, so their total volume c₁.side³ + c₂.side³ = 2s³ is bounded by volumeSum = 1. `collision_side_le_half_cbrt` immediately gives s³ ≤ 1/2.
mathContext: If two distinct cubes with the same side length $s$ appear in a VolumeDissection, they each contribute $s^3$ to the sum $\sum c_i^3 = 1$. Since all other terms are nonneg, $2s^3 \leq 1$, i.e., $s \leq 2^{-1/3} \approx 0.7937$. This is a quantitative upper bound on how large any repeated-size cube can be in a volume-constrained dissection.

title: Structural Lemmas: Minimum Cube Count and Volume Additivity
content: `min_cubes_for_collision` proves any dissection with a collision pair has ≥ 2 cubes: extract the pair (c₁, c₂), form the 2-element subset {c₁, c₂}, compute its cardinality via `Finset.card_insert_of_notMem` and `hne`, then apply `Finset.card_le_card` to bound the dissection's card from below. `volumeSum_union` proves additivity over disjoint unions by unfolding to `Finset.sum_union`. `volumeSum_eq` is a trivial `rfl` lemma providing an explicit rewrite rule to replace `volumeSum cubes` with `∑ c ∈ cubes, c.side ^ 3`.
mathContext: For a collision pair $(c_1, c_2)$ with $c_1 \neq c_2$ both in $D$: $|D| \geq |\{c_1, c_2\}| = 2$. Volume additivity: for disjoint $A, B \subseteq \text{Cube}$, $V(A \cup B) = V(A) + V(B)$. This mirrors the measure-theoretic fact that volume is additive on disjoint sets, here at the discrete level of Finsets.

title: Satisfiability: The One-Cube Witness and Decomposition Lemmas
content: `volume_constraint_satisfiable` exhibits a VolumeDissection: one cube with side=1 at the origin. The proof checks: (1) covers_unit_cube is trivially True; (2) the cube is in [0,1]³; (3) volumeSum {c} = c.side³ = 1³ = 1. Supporting lemmas `volumeSum_union` and `volumeSum_eq` establish that the volume sum is additive over disjoint unions and equals a scalar-multiple formula. The one-cube witness is the trivial dissection — the unit cube itself — which satisfies the volume constraint but trivially (no proper dissection).
mathContext: Witness: $D = \{\text{cube with side} = 1\}$, $\text{volumeSum}(D) = 1^3 = 1$. Decomposition: $\text{volumeSum}(A \cup B) = \text{volumeSum}(A) + \text{volumeSum}(B)$ for disjoint $A, B$ (Finset.sum_union).
